balanced_closed_case: Start at s and repeatedly follow an unused outgoing token.
At any non-start packet reached by an unused incoming token, total OUT=IN implies an unused outgoing token remains until the walk returns to its start; hence a maximal walk closes.
Remove the used closed walk tokens. Residual IN and OUT remain equal at every packet.
If tokens remain, connected positive support implies some packet on the accumulated closed history is incident to residual support; residual balance supplies an outgoing residual token there.
Build another finite closed history from that packet and splice it at the shared occurrence.
Each splice consumes at least one previously unused token, so finitely many repetitions consume all N_T tokens.
constructive_finite_proof.external_analogy_only: This is analogous to the finite directed Euler-trail construction, but the external name is not a premise.
open_case: When s!=t, add one formal auxiliary proof-token alpha:t->s. This token is NOT a native transition and requires no adjacency assertion.
The augmented finite token system has equal OUT and IN at every active packet and remains relationally connected.
Construct a closed token history by the closed-case procedure.

Cut the unique auxiliary alpha token and rotate the remaining token order to start immediately after alpha. The resulting raw history starts at s, ends at t, uses every original token exactly once, and uses no auxiliary token.
constructive_finite_proof.termination: Finite because each iteration consumes a positive number of the N_T original transition tokens.
constructive_finite_proof.tokenization: Replace each multiplicity T(x,y) by exactly T(x,y) distinguishable proof-tokens x->y. All non-auxiliary tokens are declared adjacency transitions.

definitions.symmetrized_positive_support: x ~_T y iff T(x,y)+T(y,x)>0; connectivity means finite relational reachability on ACTIVE(T), not metric/geometric connectivity

facts: no positive-transition history can start at C and realize T

positive_transition_case.candidate_correction: Balance plus connected ACTIVE(T) alone is insufficient in the closed case if the declared basepoint s=t is inactive.
iff_conditions: Every positive T(x,y) is on declared adjacency.
ACTIVE(T) is connected under the symmetrized positive-transition support relation.
If s=t, then s belongs to ACTIVE(T). For s!=t, endpoint activity follows from the balance law.
positive_transition_case.weakest_endpoint_activity_clause: Only the closed case needs an explicit basepoint-activity clause; for s!=t the balance law forces s,t active.

zero_transition_case.iff: N_T=0 is realizable with endpoints (s,t) iff s=t.

well_typed_table_requirement: Every positive T(x,y) must correspond to declared ADJACENCY(x,y); otherwise F(T;s,t)=empty.
